title: Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey vetoes driverless rideshare ordinance
key_facts: On Thursday (1 Oct 2026) the Minneapolis City Council passed, 7 to 6, an ordinance requiring a human in the driver’s seat of a robotaxi.
Mayor Jacob Frey sent the council a letter on Friday (2 Oct 2026) vetoing it.
Supporters said it would focus on safety and protect thousands of rideshare drivers from losing their jobs to autonomous vehicles.
Frey said a human monitor cancels the benefits for riders who prefer a driverless car, citing testimony from the disability community and concerns about crimes by drivers and passengers.
Frey said the ordinance does not address emergency response, privacy, traffic enforcement, liability and insurance, and called it a "back door ban".
The council could override the veto but needs nine votes; seven members voted for the ordinance and six against.
Frey said he is ready to work with the council on an ordinance covering both safety concerns and practicalities.
quote_evidence: Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey vetoed an ordinance passed by the City Council to regulate autonomous rideshare vehicles.

why_it_matters_hint: The veto leaves driverless rideshare allowed in Minneapolis unless the council finds two more votes or rewrites the rules.
event_date: Veto letter Friday 2 Oct 2026; council vote Thursday 1 Oct 2026
notes: Follow-up of the 2 Oct edition item (C11-07: "Minneapolis City Council approves driverless rideshares ordinance; Mayor Frey says he’ll veto"). New today: the veto itself and the nine-vote override threshold. The 7 yes votes versus 9 needed is our arithmetic from CBS’s vote list.
